reconcile.connective: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown harmonize the verses by reading Jeremiah as narrating what Chronicles leaves untold: Nebuchadnezzar changed his plan and killed Jehoiakim en route to Babylon, leaving him unburied outside Jerusalem.

discrepancy.connective: The sharpest press of the discrepancy comes from Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible, which reads Chronicles' fettering-for-Babylon and Jeremiah's denial of any burial as flatly incompatible claims about where Jehoiakim died.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com, est. 1999)

excerpts.excerpt_text: But Ch2 36:6 states that “Nebuchadnezzar bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon”; his treatment there is nowhere mentioned. The prophecy here, and in Jer 36:30, harmonizes these two facts. He was slain by Nebuchadnezzar, who changed his purpose of taking him to Babylon, on the way thither, and left him unburied outside Jerusalem.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles 2 Chronicles 36:6's fettering-for-Babylon with Jeremiah 22:19's denial of burial: argues Jehoiakim never reached Babylon, having died en route and been left exposed near Jerusalem instead.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pairing (2 Chron. 36:6 vs. Jer. 22:19/36:30, 2 Kings 24:6) under 'Historical Discrepancies' (pp. 374-375), surveying Bertheau/Hasse/Movers (the Hebrew infinitive implies Jehoiakim was not actually carried to Babylon), Bleek (slain outside the city), and Rawlinson (bound with intent, slain instead, later interred with his fathers).

link.title: 2 Chronicles 36:6—Was Jehoiakim carried to Babylon or did he die in Jerusalem?
